title: Toast wraps at half the viewport width on phones: tall broken pill over content
devices: iPhone (all phones); also iPad/Mac for long toasts (wraps at 410/735px)
evidence: shots/shell/toast-iphone.png; eval rect [100.5,735.5,201,78.5]; css/components.css:389-405 (#toast: position fixed; inset-inline-start:50%; translate(-50%) with shrink-to-fit width)
rootCause: A fixed element with left:50% gets an available width of (viewport - 50%) for shrink-to-fit sizing, so text wraps at 50% of the viewport before the max-inline-size ever applies.
fix: Give the toast an explicit fit-content width independent of its left offset: e.g. inset-inline:0; margin-inline:auto; inline-size:fit-content; max-inline-size:min(var(--toast-max), calc(100% - var(--sp-32))); transform only on Y. Use a rounded-rect radius (r-16) when it wraps, or keep pill only for one line.
detail: Any toast longer than ~25 characters on iPhone wraps into a 201px-wide, 3-line 'pill' (radius pill on a tall box) sitting over the page content above the tab bar. Reproduced with KOS.ui.toast('You already had 44 badge tiers — they are on the Badge Wall.') at 402x874: rect x=100.5 w=201 h=78.5. Same on every width: the toast can never be wider than half the viewport.

title: Global Backspace = Back fires even when a page handled the key: Backspace on a Money row opens 'Delete this entry?' AND navigates to the previous page underneath
evidence: shots/shell/backspace-money-dialog-over-home.png; eval result {hash:'#/home', dialog:'Delete this entry? QA coffee, −£4.50…'}; js/main.js:20-28; js/modules/money.js:610
rootCause: The shell's history shortcut ignores defaultPrevented and treats any non-text target as free to navigate.
fix: In main.js return early when e.defaultPrevented, when a dialog is open, or when the target is inside [role=listbox]/[data-keys]; better, drop bare Backspace and keep Alt+←/→ (and ⌘[ / ⌘] on the Mac). Register the listener in the bubble phase after page handlers (it already is) and respect defaultPrevented.
detail: js/main.js binds Backspace (outside text fields) to KOS.back() on document and never checks e.defaultPrevented. Money's transaction list uses Delete/Backspace on a focused row to delete it (money.js:610) and calls preventDefault, but the document listener still runs: reproduced on #/money/transactions → focus a row → Backspace: the confirm dialog opens while the route has already changed to #/home behind it; cancelling leaves the user on Home, having lost their place. Any future in-page Backspace handler (ink lasso selection, lists, the editor's rows, Mind's list at mindui.js:154 which is inside a textarea so is safe) collides the same way. Backspace-as-Back is also surprising on its own: a stray Backspace with focus on any button (after clicking a card, closing a menu) leaves the page; browsers removed this shortcut for that reason.

title: KOS.rerender() throws the page back to the top on every device: it saves/restores #main.scrollTop but #stage is the scroller
evidence: eval: {'#/home': ['stage', 600, 0]}; eval reminders {b:[900,0], afterRerender:0, after Back: 0}; scroller probe: #stage overflow-y auto (scrollHeight 2152 / client 772), #main overflow visible; js/core/ui.js:353-356 (var top = main.scrollTop … main.scrollTop = top), js/core/ui.js:1521-1523 (main.innerHTML = ''; main.scrollTop = 0); iPhone eval ['stage',800,0]
rootCause: The scroll container moved from #main to #stage (layout) but ui.js still saves/restores #main.scrollTop, which is always 0.
fix: Introduce one KOS.ui.scrollRoot() (the #stage on wide layouts, document.scrollingElement on the phone) and use it in rerender (save before, restore after the view drew, and again on the next frame for async content) and in show() (reset to 0 on a real navigation; restore a remembered position per history index on Back/Forward, like the router already keeps args per index). Add a smoke test.
detail: Every non-navigation redraw (cloud pull, routine auto-tick, achievements touch, Google/Todoist cycle, a goal or money tick, the day review, and 144 KOS.rerender() call sites in 30 files, many after an in-page action) resets the scroll position. Reproduced at 1470x832: #/home scrolled to 600 → KOS.rerender() → 0; #/reminders scrolled to 900 → KOS.rerender() → 0. Browser Back to a long page also lands at the top (reminders 900 → Home → Back → 0). This contradicts the router contract ('a background pull that repaints the page you are on leaves … your scroll position exactly as they were', router.js:25-29, invariant 65) and the standing 'lost position on redraw' rule. Same on iPhone (402x874: #/home 800 → 0, #stage is the scroller there too).

title: Weekly/monthly reports saved before the history arrives are frozen as 'A quiet week for study' forever
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/home-reports/seed-home-mac-all-desks.png (Week in review card 0m beside Study hours 9.2); eval KOS.reportStore.cached(): week:2026-10-19 {mins:0,sessions:0} created 1793576817945; ledger has type focus on 2026-10-20..25; js/core/reportstore.js:228-231 (hasContent counts plan/tasks), :275-279 (latest week always saved, a saved report is never rebuilt)
rootCause: Save-once reports are created from an incomplete ledger; hasContent treats seeded Pacing rows as activity.
fix: Do not let plan/tasks alone make a rebuilt week 'content'; hold the first ensureReports until the first cloud pull has completed (or until KOS.cloud says signed-out), and after importFull / first cloud link re-run the backfill with a 'replace rebuilt reports whose facts are empty or older than the newest ledger entry in their period' rule (rebuilt reports were never shown as final anyway).
detail: ensureReports() runs at boot and saves every backfilled week since 1 September. The skip rule for an empty rebuilt week is hasContent(), which counts f.plan and f.tasks; the shipped Pacing seed gives every fresh install plan facts, and the LATEST week is saved whatever it holds. So the first boot on an empty device (a new iPad/iPhone before sign-in finishes its first pull, or before a backup is restored with importFull, which does not touch kurenai-os-reports) saves weeks with mins:0 and the month 'October 2026 · a quiet month for study'. Reports are never recomputed (getReport hit -> skip), so after the history arrives Home's Reports card still says 'A quiet week for study · 0m studied' while Study hours on the same screen shows 9.2 h and the ledger has focus sessions on 20, 21, 22, 23 and 25 Oct. Reproduced: reset -> first boot -> seed: week:2026-10-19 and week:2026-10-12 both have facts.study.mins 0, createdAt = the reset boot, while weeks saved during the seed have real minutes.

title: iPhone Seat: showcase medals draw at 80px over each other and the XP bar, and the empty slots are 17 x 44 ovals
evidence: shots/achievements-governor/iphone_gov.png (six ovals), iphone_gov_ovals_crop.png (2x: 80px medals overlapping each other and the XP bar, two oval empties); eval: medals [32,580,80,80,'80px'], [80,580,80,80], [128,580,80,80]; slots [44,44]x3 + [17,44]x3; note width 131 while empty; js/modules/governor-ui.js:363-366, css/views/governor.css:518-523
rootCause: Inline custom property beats the phone stylesheet; empty flex-basis:100% note squeezes the shrinkable slots
fix: Set the medal size through a class/attribute (data-size) or `--m` on the slot and read it with var() fallback, or override with `.k-gv-arc-slot .k-ach-medal { --m: var(--ach-medal-sm) !important }` at <=700; give slots flex: 0 0 auto (no shrink) and hide the empty note (`.k-gv-arc-note:empty { display:none }`).
detail: At 402px the arc becomes a flex row of 44px slots. (1) Filled slots carry the medal with an inline --m:80px (governor-ui.js passes px:80), which beats the phone rule `.k-gv-arc-slot .k-ach-medal { --m: var(--ach-medal-sm) }`, so three picked medals render 80 x 80 at x=32/80/128, overlapping one another and rising over the XP bar. (2) The empty .k-gv-arc-note keeps flex-basis:100% while the row does not wrap (the wrap rule only applies when the note has content), so it takes 131px and the empty slots shrink to 17 x 44 (ovals); before the list() call returns, all six are ovals.

title: A ping shows on top of the unlock overlay (and above any dialog) when a tier and a ping arrive in the same sweep
evidence: shots/achievements-governor/seed_governor.png (ping at top left over the 'Regular III' unlock overlay); eval: .k-ach-pings z-index 130 vs .k-ach-unlock-overlay 120; js/modules/achievements.js:760-765, 684-689
rootCause: Overlay opening is async while ping is sync; quiet() only checks dialogs already in the DOM
fix: In onChange, skip pings when r.earned.length (the overlay is about to open), or have ping() also check a module-level `showing`/queue.length; drainPing should re-check quiet() before each ping.
detail: Invariant 163 says the ping never shows while a dialog is open. In boot()'s onChange, celebrate(r.earned) only queues the overlay (drain() waits for the async A().list), then r.pings.forEach(ping) runs immediately; quiet() sees no dialog yet, so the ping appears. It sits at z-index var(--z-toast) (130) above the overlay scrim (120), at the top-left over the dimmed page while the unlock overlay is up.

title: 'Owned' means two different things: the Wall header and the Seat say 8 badges while the set panels and the Showcase show 21

title: Every Wall tab (and the Seat's showcase arc) waits 1.6-6 s on 'Reading your records…' because list() re-walks the whole vault each time
evidence: shots/achievements-governor/seed_showcase.png (blank 'Reading your records…' after 1.5 s); eval list() 4744 ms then 1623 ms; per-set timings above; js/core/achcatalogue.js:70-110 (openCursor over entries), js/core/achievements.js:329-341 (fresh makeCtx per list)
rootCause: Achievements are measured on read with no memo across calls; the Collection reader is a full-table cursor
fix: Cache the last evaluation's views (evaluate() already measures everything at boot and every 30 min and on owner touches) and draw the Wall from that cache immediately, refreshing in the background; for the vault, keep running tallies keyed on the vault's change notes or read counts through indexes (status/module) instead of a full cursor.
detail: Each Wall draw (Sets, Recent, Showcase, Titles, every tab switch since each is a KOS.show) calls KOS.achievements.list(), which makes a fresh context and re-measures all 254 badges; the Collection badges open an unbounded IndexedDB cursor over every vault entry (1,880 rows on the seeded account) and tally them. Timed on the seeded account: list() 1.6-4.7 s; per set sequentially: collection 6.5 s, exams 1.8 s, study 1.4 s, mind 1.3 s. Showcase still read 'Reading your records…' after 1.5 s. It also conflicts with invariant 8 (never read an unbounded collection).

title: KOS.rerender() never keeps the scroll position: it saves #main.scrollTop but #stage is the scroller, so every cloud pull jumps the page to the top
evidence: harness eval sd3.js: ipad {st1:900,st2:0,h1:700,h2:0,a1:1500,a2:0}; mac {st1:530,st2:0,...}; iphone same. Code: js/core/ui.js:353-356 (var main=getElementById('main'); var top=main.scrollTop; ... main.scrollTop=top); KOS.show resets main.scrollTop=0 at js/core/ui.js:1526
rootCause: rerender measured the wrong element after the shell moved scrolling to #stage
fix: Save/restore the real scroller (#stage, or a KOS.shell.scroller() helper that returns the element whose overflow scrolls, including the phone shell) and restore AFTER the view has rendered (and once more after async content lands, e.g. on next rAF / after vault lazy batch). Better: part of the redraw policy below — background redraws should not happen while the user is reading.
detail: KOS.rerender (the cloud-pull/background redraw path) reads and restores document.getElementById('main').scrollTop, but the element that actually scrolls is #stage (#main has overflow visible; on the iPad #main.scrollHeight 2406 vs #stage 2406/1120 scrolling). KOS.show then empties #main, the height collapses and the browser clamps #stage.scrollTop to 0. Repro (seeded account): open compsci 4.5.2.1, set #stage.scrollTop=900, KOS.rerender() -> 0. Same on Home (700 -> 0) and the Anime vault (1500 -> 0) at mac, ipad and iphone sizes. So any pull, merge, auto-ticked habit, Daily Review close etc. throws the reader back to the top of the page.

title: CS/Maths/IT notes reset to page 1 on every background redraw (the reported 'notes page 4 jumps back to page 1')

title: A background redraw mid-flashcards restarts the set at card 1 and silently drops the cards already rated from the session ledger (no XP, no streak credit)
evidence: harness eval (ipad): topic log ['18 left of 18 What is a number base?', ..., '15 left of 18'] -> afterFront '18 left of 18 What is a number base?'; due {d3life:'This session: 0 again · 0 hard · 3 good · 0 easy', dAfterLife:''}. js/engines/flashcards.js:295-322 (rate keeps counts in closure, store.save only), :325-355 (finish is the only KOS.sessions.log), :356 restart
rootCause: session progress and the pay-at-finish rule live in DOM-bound closures

(2) Keep an in-progress review session in a per-device session store (state.ui.fcSession[deckKey] = {queue keys, graduated, counts, startedAt}) and resume it on remount. (3) Log/bank the partial batch on unmount/pagehide (like Focus banks its clock, invariant 4c) so pay never depends on the DOM surviving.
detail: The flashcard engine keeps queue, graduated and counts in its mount closure, and only logs the review session in finish(). A KOS.rerender mid-set remounts it: on a topic's Flashcards tab the queue is rebuilt from ALL the topic's cards, so the learner is put back on card 1 and re-meets cards they just rated (re-rating them applies FSRS's short-term rule again, skewing their schedule); on Due today the counts reset ('This session: 0 again · 0 hard · 3 good' -> ''), and because a session is only logged at finish(), the ratings made before the redraw never produce a session entry — their XP/gold and the study-streak credit are lost (the SRS schedule itself was saved). Due today: rate 3 ('304 left of 307', life line 3 good) -> after rerender '304 left of 304', life line empty.

title: Every cloud pull/merge redraws the active view unconditionally — even when nothing the view shows changed, and even while the user is mid-task
devices: iPad primarily (app switching + Pencil study), all
evidence: js/core/cloudsync.js:487-497 (mergeRemoteIn -> rerenderCurrent), :723-733 (rerenderCurrent -> KOS.rerender), :773-777, :533-560 (conflict path), :1447-1459 (noteChange push), :1480-1495 (Realtime), :1541-1553 (interval/visible/focus); js/core/ui.js:344-357 (rerender: only inkUI.busy guard). Harness: KOS.rerender() reproduces every reset in the other findings.
rootCause: full remount used as the generic refresh for background state changes, with no busy/changed gating
fix: Systemic redraw policy: (1) cloudsync passes what changed (top-level keys that differ between pre- and post-merge state, cheap JSON compare per key) to KOS.rerender({changed:[...], background:true}); views declare the state keys they read (KOS.views.x.reads = ['srs','edits',...]) and are skipped when untouched. (2) A background redraw is DEFERRED while the page is 'busy': a dialog or menu open, focus in an input/textarea/contenteditable, a study engine mounted and touched in the last N minutes (flashcards/quiz/exam/japanese session/code task), pointer down, or within 30 s of the last interaction — instead show a quiet 'Updated on another device · Refresh' chip, and redraw on the next navigation. (3) For views that must refresh live, give them a refresh(changed) hook that patches in place instead of a full remount.
detail: cloudsync.rerenderCurrent() calls KOS.rerender() after every applied remote state: the clean path (applyRemoteState, cloudsync.js:775), the merge path (mergeRemoteIn, :495, also used by a push that lost its compare-and-set race, :533-560) and first link (:1279). There is no check of whether the merged document differs in anything the current view reads, no check that the user is interacting, a dialog/menu is open, an input has focus, or a study engine is running. The only guard in KOS.rerender is the ink pen (ui.js:347). Triggers that reach it: another device's push -> Realtime 'changed' (1.5 s debounce, :1483); returning to the app (visibilitychange/focus, :1548-1552, at most once a minute) — on the iPad every app switch; the 15-min interval; and the iPad's OWN ratings: each store.save -> noteChange -> push after 4 s -> if the Mac/iPhone pushed meanwhile the CAS fails -> conflict() -> mergeRemoteIn -> rerender. An idle open Mac pushes on its own (achievement sweep every 30 min, goals/notify ticks, routine auto-ticks, Daily Review words), so the iPad is redrawn under the user regularly. This is the root of the reported iPad resets.

title: Closing the Daily Review sheet (Later, Esc, Close) redraws the page underneath — and on the iPad it can auto-open over a lesson when you return to the app
evidence: shots/sync-disruption/review-close-notes-reset.png (Page 1 of 7 after close; was Page 4 of 7). eval sd8.js {before:'Page 4 of 7', open:true, after:'Page 1 of 7'}. js/modules/dayreview.js:85-93, :661, :709, :722-729 (blocked), :744-749
rootCause: overlay close uses KOS.rerender as a blanket refresh; auto-open guard only considers boot deep links
fix: Close should repaint only what the review changed (chip, Home's cards if Home is on screen) — or call the policy's refresh(changed) — never a full remount. Auto-open on visibility should only happen on Home (or when no study page/engine is active); elsewhere it waits in the chip.
detail: reviewSheet.close() calls KOS.rerender() whenever it is not silent (dayreview.js:92), as does the final Close button (:661) and Skip (:709). The overlay is outside #main, so the page under it never needed a redraw; the redraw resets notes page, flashcards, quiz, scroll. Repro iPad: compsci 4.5.4.3 notes page 4 ('Page 4 of 7'), KOS.reviewSheet.open(slot), close -> 'Page 1 of 7' (screenshot). Worse, maybeOpen() runs on every visibilitychange to visible (:749); the deep-link guard uses bootHash, which is cleared 1.5 s after boot (:746), so after boot the sheet auto-opens over ANY page (a topic, a Code lesson, Due today) when the iPad app is brought back inside a new review slot; the blocked() check knows only Focus, a dialog and the Exam Room. Dismissing it then wipes the lesson state.

title: Handwritten tab Side by side: both panes jump to the top on a background redraw (1.5 s after the pen lifts)
devices: iPad landscape (Side by side is >1080 only)
evidence: eval sd11.js (ipadl): {scrollers:['ink.side-notes 7882/744','ink.side-page 982/744'], before:[600,238], after:['ink.side-notes 0','ink.side-page 0']}. js/core/ui.js:347-351 (busy guard only), js/core/inkui.js:341

Once the pen has been lifted for 1.5 s — i.e. while the student reads the notes pane or thinks — a pull redraws the tab and both independent scroll regions reset. Repro iPad landscape (1180x820): compsci 4.5.4.3, Handwritten, Side by side; ink.side-notes scrolled to 600 and ink.side-page to 238; KOS.rerender() -> both 0. title: A background redraw steals focus from whatever is being typed in — the iPad/iPhone keyboard closes mid-sentence
evidence: eval (ipad): {active:'BODY ', val:'half a thou', sel:11}. js/core/ui.js:344-357, :1520-1541 (main.innerHTML = '' then remount); js/core/a11y.js:97 comment says a redraw must leave the reader where they are but there is no focus restore
rootCause: remount without focus/selection preservation
fix: Policy: never run a background redraw while document.activeElement is an editable element inside #main (defer until blur + idle). As a fallback, record a focus signature (data-ui + index + selection) before the redraw and restore it after (mobile-shell.js:600-640 already has calendarFocusSignature to generalise).
detail: KOS.rerender remounts #main; the focused field is destroyed and focus falls to <body>. The quick-note draft itself survives (stored per device), but the caret is gone, so on the iPad the on-screen keyboard dismisses while the user is typing; any keystrokes in flight are lost. The same applies to every inline input on any page (search filters in vaults, Money amount fields, Goals editor in-page fields, Code task editor, Writing Desk). Repro iPad: compsci 4.5.4.3, focus the quick note, type, caret at 4, KOS.rerender() -> document.activeElement BODY; the new textarea has the text but no focus (selection at end).

title: Japanese review/learn session restarts and loses its unlogged results on a background redraw
evidence: js/modules/jarun.js:361-390 (run, `var results = [], i = 0`), :434 (finishSession only at end); js/modules/japanese.js:305 (view calls run on every render); contrast js/modules/mind.js:594,662
rootCause: session state in closure + pay at finish
fix: Keep the running session (keys, index, results) per device in state.ui.japanese.run and resume on remount, or bank results incrementally; plus the redraw policy.
detail: KOS.jaRun.run keeps `results` and the index in its closure and pays only at the end (KOS.ja.finishSession(results)). A KOS.rerender on #/japanese/session/... re-runs run(): the list is rebuilt from KOS.ja.due() (facets already graded drop out) and the results so far are discarded, so the +1 XP per passed facet for them is never logged. title: A background redraw closes any open menu or popover — including the header bell, which is outside the page
evidence: eval sd6.js (ipad): {menuOpen:true, menuCls:'k-menu-panel k-nt-pop', menuAfter:false}. js/core/ui.js:1513-1519 (closeOpenMenu before every render)
rootCause: navigation clean-up applied to redraws
fix: On a redraw (KOS.ui.redrawing) keep a menu whose anchor is outside #main, and for menus inside #main defer the background redraw while a menu is open (redraw policy).

title: Edits in a Code lesson's runnable listings are lost on a background redraw

title: routines.onSession redraws the whole page whenever an auto-tracked habit ticks itself — e.g. right after a flashcard batch or Code task pass
evidence: js/core/routines.js:697-700 (onSession -> autoSync -> KOS.rerender), :672-690 (autoSync), js/engines/flashcards.js:349 (session logged at finish), js/engines/quiz.js:428 (exam item logs a session). Not reproduced end-to-end in the harness (could not get an auto habit to tick with a hand-made ledger entry); path read from code.
rootCause: blanket rerender as change notification

detail: Every logged session (flashcard batch finish, exam item marked, Code task pass, Japanese session) calls routines.onSession, which runs autoSync() and, if any auto-tracked habit ticked, KOS.rerender() (only guarded against an open dialog). So the moment a 'Review 20 cards' or '1 Code task passed' habit completes, the page that caused it is remounted: the flashcards 'Session complete' summary is replaced by a fresh deck, a Code task's passing result panel is redrawn, an exam tab returns to question 1. Only the habit chip/Home needs to change.

title: Toasts are capped at half the viewport width and, on the iPhone, sit on top of the flashcard rating buttons (and catch taps when they carry Undo)
evidence: shots/sync-disruption/toast-over-rate-iphone.png; eval sd10.js iphone {toast:[101,708,201,98], rate:[16,694,370,60], overlap:true, pe:'auto'}, ipad {toast:[205,1092,410,64]}. css/components.css:389-408, :669
rootCause: left:50% shrink-to-fit width; fixed bottom offset ignores page controls
fix: Centre with inset-inline:0; margin-inline:auto; inline-size:fit-content (keep max-inline-size), and on study pages lift the toast above the active control row (or place it top-centre on phones while a study engine is mounted).
detail: #toast is positioned with inset-inline-start:50% + translate(-50%), so its shrink-to-fit width is limited to the space right of the centre line: 201 px on the iPhone (402/2) and 410 px on the iPad (820/2). A one-line message wraps to four lines (98 px tall). On the iPhone it sits 12 px above the tab bar, i.e. exactly over the Hard/Good rating buttons of a flashcard (toast 101,708 201x98 vs rate row 16,694 370x60: overlapping), and an action toast has pointer-events:auto, so a rating tap lands on the toast. title: A redraw mid-retrieval resets the Code retrieval card's tries, hint flag and clock, so the derived grade comes out better than earned
evidence: js/modules/code.js:972 (var started = Date.now(), tries = 0, hinted = false), :984 (clock), :601-611 (task clock). Code-read; the remount path is the same KOS.rerender reproduced in the other findings.
rootCause: evidence inputs held in closures
fix: Keep the in-progress attempt (tries, hinted, startedAt) per card in state.ui.code.attempt[key] until it is graded, and defer background redraws while a retrieval is open.
detail: Code retrieval grades are derived from tries, hints and time (invariant 107, never self-reported), but the card keeps `started`, `tries` and `hinted` in its render closure. After a failed try and an opened hint, a background redraw remounts the card with tries=0, hinted=false and a fresh clock; passing then records a clean, fast first-try grade and schedules the card too far out. Task timers (code.js:601) reset the same way.

title: After a background redraw the open dialog's opener is detached, so closing it drops focus to <body>

title: Boot-time redraws of whatever page the PWA reopened on (Google read-only copy, own art pictures, sample seed)
evidence: js/core/ext.js:364; js/main.js:299-307
rootCause: KOS.rerender used as a broadcast
fix: Have these refresh only the views that read them (Calendar for loadRo; the art slots via KOS.art.apply/paint, which artslot.js already does in place) instead of a full remount.
detail: Three boot paths call KOS.rerender() on the current page after async work: KOS.ext boot when Google Calendar is connected (ext.js:364, after loadRo from IndexedDB), KOS.art.loadOwn (main.js:307) and the sample seed (main.js:299-304). The iPad Home Screen app restores the last route (e.g. a topic), so the page the user has just started reading or tapping is remounted a moment after launch, for data (Google's read-only chips, decorative art) that only Calendar or a painted slot needs.

title: Inconsistent refresh policy: Google/Todoist pulls change Calendar and Reminders without redrawing them, while a state pull redraws every page
evidence: js/core/ext.js:325-337 (syncAll -> changed()), :294; js/modules/connections.js:173-177 (the only listener); js/core/extgcal.js and exttasks.js contain no redraw
rootCause: no domain-scoped change notification
fix: Introduce one change bus (KOS.changed(domains)) fired by cloudsync (with the keys that differed), ext, routines, inksync, files; views subscribe by domain and refresh in place (or defer while busy).
detail: KOS.ext.syncAll (every cycle and the 1.5 s 'soon' sync) writes pulled events and reminders through the owners, then only notifies KOS.ext.onChange listeners — only the Connections page listens. An open Calendar or Reminders page keeps showing the old data (a task completed in Todoist stays unticked on screen) until the user navigates, whereas a cloud state pull remounts any page however unrelated. There is no single 'state changed → which views care' mechanism.

title: Specification tab shows garbled PDF-extraction text on most Maths leaves (M7.3 included)
evidence: shots/content-maths/m73-spec-mac.png; shots/content-maths/p5-6-spec-mac.png; cm/spine.txt (every leaf's spec text); tools/gen_data.py:240-255 (maths_group copies clean(x) of the extracted lines)

Examples: M7.3 guidance reads "v = u + at r = ut +1at2 / e.g. , with vectors / 2 given in i - j or column vector form". 5.6 reads "Understand and use double a n g le f / rm u l a e ; u s e / f s in ( A ± B ), fo r m u l a e fo r / ± ± cos (A B)". 2.1 reads "× = , ÷ = - , = m n n am / The equivalence ofa and should be known." 2.10 starts mid-sentence: "into partial fractions". 25 leaves still contain the extraction artefact "need to learn:" or "students need to learn:". title: Quiz answers are almost always A or B, and options are never shuffled
evidence: cm/metrics.json ansDist per leaf; js/engines/quiz.js:66 (Shuffle shuffles order only), :88-96 (item.opts rendered in order, answer compared to item.ans at :113); e.g. js/data/content/maths-mech-m7.js:305-306 (every item ans: 0); shots/content-maths/m73-quiz-ipad.png (Q1 answer A)
rootCause: Authors put the right answer first (bank authors second), and the engine trusts the authored order.
fix: In mountMCQ, shuffle a per-question option permutation at mount and on Retry, seeded per attempt, and map clicks back to the original index so the stats and the why text stay valid. Optionally also rebalance the authored ans positions so a fixed order is fair too.
detail: Of 1,058 Maths quiz items, the correct option is A in 531 and B in 481. Only 44 are C and 2 are D. Base files: 380 A, 100 B, 17 C, 1 D. Bank files: 151 A, 381 B, 27 C, 1 D. KOS.quiz.mountMCQ renders opts in authored order, and its Shuffle button only reorders the questions. A learner soon learns to pick A on a base item or B on a bank item, so the quiz score stops measuring understanding. Separately, the correct option is uniquely the longest in 317 items (30%).

title: "Write it out" chip overlaps worked-example titles on every device and is only 23px tall

title: Santander midata CSV is refused: 'Merchant/Description' and 'Debit/Credit' headers are not recognised

rootCause: Exact-match header regexes plus a hard gate before the manual mapper.

detail: The midata export's header 'Date,Type,Merchant/Description,Debit/Credit,Balance' maps only Date; GUESS has no pattern for 'Merchant/Description' (payee) or 'Debit/Credit' (signed amount), so read() fails with 'It has no header row with a date and an amount.' before the user ever reaches the column mapper, even though the mapper could have fixed it by hand. title: Import only reads the first line as the header: midata with a leading blank line or a semicolon delimiter, and Online Banking CSV with an account preamble, all fail
evidence: js/core/money.js:947-969; browser repro of 6 sample files (midata-semicolon.csv delimiter ',' header one cell; santander-online-excel.csv header ['Account:',…]); all dialogAccepts=false
rootCause: Header = rows[0], delimiter sniffed from text.split(/\r?\n/)[0].
fix: Detect the delimiter over the first ~10 non-empty lines; scan the first 20 rows for the first row that matches date+amount header patterns and treat everything above as preamble (show it as 'Skipped: 3 header lines'); drop trailing empty columns.
detail: parseCSV picks the delimiter from line 1 only (a leading blank line forces ','), and takes rows[0] as the header. Santander midata variants (';' delimited, trailing ';', blank first line) parse into one column; the Online Banking CSV/Excel export starts with 'Account:'/'From:' preamble lines so the header is 'Account:,Santander…'. All refused with the same generic message.

title: Santander's other exports (.txt, QIF, OFX) are not supported at all; the picker accepts .txt but cannot read it

rootCause: Single CSV parser path.
fix: Add format sniffing: OFX/QFX (parse STMTTRN, use FITID as the dedupe key, LEDGERBAL to reconcile), QIF (D/T/P/M/^ records), the Santander .txt block format; name the format detected in the Columns step. Keep CSV for everything else.
detail: Online Banking 'Download transactions' offers text (Date:/Description:/Amount:/Balance: blocks with non-breaking spaces), Excel CSV, Quicken QIF and Microsoft Money OFX. The importer is CSV-only, yet the file input accepts text/plain, so the user's .txt is taken and fails with 'It has no header row with a date and an amount.' OFX would also give a stable FITID for exact de-duplication.

title: No way to see, undo or replace an import after the result dialog closes

rootCause: Batch metadata is not stored anywhere but on rows; UI only exposes it in a transient dialog.

detail: Each import has a batch id, but 'Undo this import' exists only on the Done step of the dialog (money.js:915). Once closed there is no import history, no filter by source/batch in Transactions (list() filters kind/cat/tag/search only), and bulk select has no 'select all' over a range, so removing a bad 200-row import means ticking rows one by one.

title: Unquoted thousands separators shift columns: '£1,234.56' imports silently as £1.00
evidence: js/core/money.js:947-969 (no per-row width check), 1005-1013; eval repro: row ['2026-10-27','in',100,'STUDENT FINANCE ENGLAND SLC']; shots/money-goals/tx-dups-all-mac.png shows +£1.00

title: A recurring rule's 'Confirm' and an imported bank row for the same payment double-count
evidence: js/core/money.js:414-433 (confirm creates tx unconditionally), 1025-1031 (dedupe by exact payee); recurring page shows Google One 'Due' for Sep/Oct even though the user has bank rows for them (shots/money-goals/recurring-mac.png)
rootCause: Rules and imports are two independent writers of the same real-world payment.
fix: On import, match rows to due occurrences (same amount ±0, date within ±3 days, payee alias set on the rule) and MARK the occurrence done pointing at the imported tx instead of creating a new one; on Confirm, offer 'Use the bank entry from 27 Oct' when one matches.
detail: Confirming an occurrence (Google One £1.59, Phone £10) writes its own transaction r:<rule>:<date> with payee = rule name; importing the bank statement then adds 'GOOGLE *Google One, ON 27-10-2026' £1.59 as a separate row. Neither side looks at the other: preview's dedupe compares payee text ('google one' vs the bank string) and confirm() never searches existing transactions. Spend, budgets, Safe to spend and Reports count the payment twice. This is a second path to the duplicates the user saw.

title: Imported rows are unusable as information: raw bank strings, everything in Other, Type and Balance columns discarded
evidence: js/core/money.js:1019-1021 (cat = other), 1041; grep of money.js/modules/money.js finds no merchant/auto-category code; shots/money-goals/tx-dups-all-mac.png
rootCause: Import engine was built as a column copier ('the pages are phase 2' comment at money.js:946).
fix: Revamp (see summary): store raw text, derive a clean merchant (strip 'CARD PAYMENT TO', '(VIA APPLE PAY)', ', ON dd-mm-yyyy', ',n.nn GBP, RATE …', store numbers, title-case); payee rules {match -> merchant, category} learned when the user sets a category ('Always put Heron Foods in Food?'); a built-in UK merchant table (Tesco, Heron Foods, Greggs, Stagecoach, Google, Spotify, SLC…); Type DD/SO -> suggest a recurring rule; Balance -> reconcile and show 'Matches the bank: £120.10'.
detail: Every imported row lands in Other/Other income (preview opts.outCat), payee is the raw bank text ('HERON FOODS HOYLAND (VIA APPLE PAY), ON 29-10-2026', 'CARD PAYMENT TO …,3.45 GBP, RATE 1.00/GBP ON …'), so Overview's 'This month by category' is one 'Other' bar, the Selected card shows a 4-line shouting title, spend-by-merchant is impossible and nothing learns from the user's re-categorising. The bank's Type (DEB/DD/FPI/FPO/SO) and Balance columns are dropped, so direct debits are not detected and the import cannot be reconciled. There is no merchant normalisation, no payee->category memory and no recurring detection anywhere in money.js.

title: iPhone: Money's Transactions, Month and year, Import/Export CSV and Goals' This week/This month/Done are unreachable

title: Painted page header shows the PREVIOUS page's picture (Goals shows Money's jar, Money shows Goals' mountain)
evidence: js/core/ui.js:589-592 (reads ui.view), js/core/ui.js:1540-1543 (view set after render); eval sequence output: '#/goals => app.hero.page.money.webp', '#/money/budgets => app.hero.page.goals.webp'; shots/money-goals/goals-mac.png (jar on Goals)
rootCause: Ordering in KOS.show: state.ui.view assigned after render.
fix: Set KOS.store.state.ui.view (or a transient KOS.ui.rendering = viewId) before calling KOS.views[viewId], or have pageHeader take the view id from the router's current call.
detail: KOS.ui.pageHeader picks its art from KOS.store.state.ui.view, but KOS.show only sets ui.view AFTER the view function has rendered. So the first render of any page that relies on PAGE_ART draws the art of the page you came from; a redraw on the same page then corrects it. Reproduced: money -> goals gives app.hero.page.money.webp on Goals; goals -> money/budgets gives app.hero.page.goals.webp on Money. Affects every page in PAGE_ART (Review, Assignments, Exams, Pacing, Calendar, Reminders, Routines, Goals, Money, Wishlist, Governor, Reports, Archive...).

title: Marks by question: a question added with '＋ Question' can't be given its Max or its topic
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/exams-files-ink/seed-marks-addq-ipad.png, audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/exams-files-ink/seed-marks-ipad.png; js/modules/examprac.js:410 addRow pushes {max:null, refs:[]}; :436-438 the row renders node title (read-only) and q.max as text; js/modules/tracker.js:192 questions only come from an index fill
rootCause: Marks page was built around index-filled questions; addRow never got editors for max/refs

title: A transparent PNG pasted or dropped onto an ink page gets a black background
evidence: js/core/inkui.js:1400-1413 (c.toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.86) with no fill first); compare js/core/imagecrop.js:110-124 which keeps PNG/WebP or fills a background before JPEG
rootCause: Unconditional JPEG encoding of user pictures
fix: Keep image/png when the source is PNG/WebP/GIF (or when the canvas has any alpha < 255), or fill the canvas white before drawImage when JPEG is chosen.
detail: readImage() in inkui.js draws every picture (paste, drop, Image… from the palette) onto a canvas and keeps it as toDataURL('image/jpeg'). JPEG has no alpha, so every transparent pixel becomes black: a diagram, a screenshot with transparency or a cut-out pasted onto a lined page shows a black box behind it on the paper.

evidence: shots/assistant-archive/chat-send-signedout-mac.png; shots/assistant-archive/memory-mac.png; js/core/ai.js:152,154; js/modules/assistant.js:2299; js/core/cloud.js:142-143; js/core/gameapi.js:23,25; js/core/vndb.js:112,281; js/core/ui.js:430-438 (Archive strip names)
rootCause: Navigation text duplicated in many string literals instead of one link helper; page renamed in review A
fix: Name it as the UI does ('Archive › Backup & Restore › Account & Cloud Sync') and render an inline 'Sign in' action on the Assistant error card and the Memory/History empty states that opens #/data with the email field focused. Signed out with no Ollama model, show a one-line notice above the composer before the first send instead of failing after it.
detail: The Assistant's failure card (signed out, the default Gemini route), Memory's empty state, cloud.js, gameapi.js and vndb.js all say 'Archive → Account & Cloud Sync'. The Archive has no page of that name: the strip reads Backup & Restore, Help & Guide, Notifications, Files, Storage, Pen and ink, Connections; the card is a section inside Backup & Restore. Connections calls it 'Open Backup & cloud'. None of the Assistant's messages is a link. A first-time user who types a question gets 'Kurenai couldn't finish that' with directions to a page they cannot find, while the status pill still says 'Kurenai is with you' with a green dot.

title: Activity (signed out) shows every action as 'Proposed … Started' forever, with no time
evidence: shots/assistant-archive/activity-after-mac.png (after a todo_add_task that the chat reported complete). js/modules/assistant.js:2587-2590 (filter r.kind === 'insert'); js/core/aiorchestrator.js:232-250 (status changes are separate 'update' rows; the insert payload has no created_at)
rootCause: Queue reader ignores update rows; insert payload lacks a timestamp
fix: When reading the queue, fold each 'update' patch into its insert by id and use the queue entry's ts as created_at.
detail: Signed out, Activity reads the local audit queue but keeps only the 'insert' rows and drops every 'update' (executed/declined/failed), so an action that ran reads 'Proposed', 'todo_add_task · proposed' and '● Started' in one row. The queued rows have no created_at, so the 'when' column is an empty 100px gap at the row's left. The filters Ran / Declined / Failed never match anything signed out.

An eyebrow is for two-word labels; this is a sentence and is the same text the chat already shows in its error card.

'done' is the raw status, '#1' an internal record id, and 'todo_add_task' the function name. title: Todoist: a reminder made on one device is duplicated when another device syncs before the state document arrives
evidence: exp/td.js twodev → local 'Made on A': [[3,'T3'],[4,'T3']], remote: ['T3']; js/core/exttasks.js:180-187 (import with no matching attempt), js/core/ext.js:306-316 (syncProvider takes the lease without pulling the cloud state first), js/core/exttasks.js:229-237
rootCause: Remote link state is replicated asynchronously while the remote cursor (sync token) is per device; import has no identity check beyond byLink.
fix: Make the cycle state-consistent: before taking the lease run a cloud pull (KOS.cloudsync cycle) and push the state right after the cycle; and in reconcile's import path, before adding, look for an existing reminder already linked to that remote id (dedupe byLink after any merge) or an unlinked one in the same list whose uuidOf('add|'+uid) is pending (record pending adds {uid→temp} in state.ext so any device can recognise its own item_add). Also add a boot/merge pass that folds two reminders linked to the same ext.id.
detail: The lease serialises Todoist network work between devices, but the LINK (reminder.ext.id) lives in the synced state document, which reaches the other device later. Device A pushes a new reminder (item_add) and links it locally; device B takes the lease next (A releases it at once) while its state still holds the reminder unlinked and its own per-device sync token predates the add. B's incremental pull returns the new Todoist task, finds no local link (byLink) and reconcile() imports it as a SECOND reminder linked to the same Todoist id; the cloud merge then keeps both (different ids/uids). Reproduced in jsdom with the smoke112 fake: after the B-side cycle, two local reminders 'Made on A' are both linked to T3 while Todoist has one task. With a Mac, iPad and iPhone all open this is the ordinary case, matching the user's 'many problems between Reminders and Todoist'.

title: Todoist: a failed second command batch leaves the first batch's tasks unlinked, so the next sync imports them as duplicates
evidence: exp/td.js chunk → 'cycle1 false Todoist answered 503 / remote items 45 local linked 0 / cycle2: local total 105 dup local 45'; js/core/exttasks.js:318-335 (ok callbacks only after the reduce over chunks resolves), js/core/exttasks.js:241-243 (token saved only after push)
rootCause: Non-atomic multi-request push with all-or-nothing local bookkeeping.
fix: Apply each chunk's results as soon as it returns (run the after[] entries whose commands are all in that chunk's sync_status), keep an item's parent and sub-task adds in one chunk, and persist the link/temp-id map before the next request; on the pull side, treat an incoming task whose id appears in a stored temp_id_mapping as already linked.
detail: tdPush sends commands in chunks of 90 and runs every 'ok' callback (which writes the link and base) only after ALL chunks succeed. If chunk 2 fails (HTTP 429/5xx, offline, tab suspended), chunk 1's item_add commands have already created tasks in Todoist but nothing local is linked, and the sync token is not saved either. The next cycle pulls those tasks with the old token, finds no local link and imports each as a new reminder; the originals are then re-sent as item_add. Linking a list with ~45+ reminders that have a sub-task each exceeds 90 commands on the first cycle. Reproduced: 60 reminders with one sub each, chunk 2 answered 503 → cycle 2 leaves 105 local reminders (45 duplicates).

title: First cloud sign-in silently discards a device's reminders, assignments, exams, routines and other data that 'stateMeaningful' does not count
evidence: exp/cs.js → {before:{rem:1,asg:1}, after:{rem:[],asg:[]}, cloudHasLocal:false}; js/core/cloudsync.js:234-251 (stateMeaningful), 975-990 (assessLink), 758-773 (not dirty → replaceState)
rootCause: A hand-maintained allowlist of 'real data' that was not extended as new domains were added; replaceState used as the adopt path.
fix: Define 'meaningful' as 'differs from a freshly booted DEFAULTS document' (hash syncableState against a boot-time pristine snapshot, ignoring known seeders such as SAMPLE events and pacing seed), or enumerate every record array in cloudmerge RECORDS plus the keyed maps; and on first link always take the no-base three-way merge (union) instead of replaceState when the local side has ANY record. Snapshot the local state into the media kv before any replaceState so it can be restored.
detail: assessLink classifies each side with stateMeaningful(), which only looks at progress, sessions, custom cards, wishlist, tracker entries, goals, non-sample calendar events and Governor xp/gold/owned. A device whose data is reminders, assignments, Exams-hub assessments, routines, Pacing ticks, Money settings, curriculum edits, Code/Japanese/Mind/Creatives evidence or SRS state (without a logged session) counts as EMPTY, so linking it to an account that has data takes the 'remoteOnly' path: adoptRemote → applyRemoteState with no lastPushedHash → dirty = stateMeaningful(local) = false → KOS.store.replaceState(incoming). The local records are replaced without a merge, a toast or a backup. Reproduced in jsdom with smoke17's fake Supabase: a fresh device adds one reminder and one assignment, signs in to an account with history; after syncNow both are gone and the cloud copy never received them. A Home Screen install on the iPad has its own storage separate from Safari, so 'used it a bit before signing in' is a realistic path. The mirror case ('localOnly' when the remote only holds such records) overwrites the remote the same way.

title: Two open tabs or windows overwrite each other's saves (last writer wins on the whole state)
devices: mac (two windows/tabs), iPad Safari with two tabs
evidence: kos.mjs eval 17 (iframe experiment) → {afterBsaved:true, finalHasA:true, finalHasB:false, inMemA_hasB:false}; js/core/store.js:395-410 (whole-document save), no 'storage' listener anywhere in js/ (grep)
rootCause: localStorage used as a single-writer store without cross-tab coordination.
fix: Listen for 'storage' on the state key and, when another tab wrote, three-way merge the incoming document into memory with KOS.cloudmerge (base = last document this tab wrote/read) before the next save; or elect one writer tab with navigator.locks / BroadcastChannel and make other tabs read-only with a banner. At minimum detect a foreign write (compare a per-save nonce) and reload instead of overwriting.
detail: Each tab keeps its own in-memory KOS.store.state and save() writes the WHOLE document to localStorage 120 ms later; nothing listens for the 'storage' event, and there is no BroadcastChannel or Web Lock. A change made in one tab is erased by the next save in the other. Reproduced on the slot with an iframe of index.html (same origin, same localStorage): tab B added 'TAB-B reminder' and saved; tab A then added its own reminder; the stored document holds A's and not B's, and tab A never learns of B's. Both tabs also mint the same nextId. With cloud sync the shared IndexedDB meta (seq, lastPushedHash, base) can let the stale tab's CAS succeed and upload a document without the other tab's record. On the MacBook a second window or a PWA window beside a tab is ordinary.

title: Todoist: a full sync drops completed sub-tasks from the reminder (and can re-add them to Todoist as duplicates)
evidence: exp/td.js subs → 'after remote sub tick: [[Plan,true],[Draft,false]]' then 'after full sync: [[Draft,false]]'; js/core/exttasks.js:217-220 (token '*' on any link change, mirror reset), 108-113 (childrenOf reads only the mirror), 296-307 (missing x → item_add)
rootCause: Absence in a full sync is interpreted as deletion.
fix: Do not reset the mirror on a full sync triggered by a link change; only drop entries of projects no longer linked. Treat a sub missing from a full sync as 'unknown', not deleted (keep subs whose remote child is not returned unless is_deleted arrives), and never re-add a sub that has an x.
detail: When the linked-project signature changes (linking or unlinking any list) the cycle requests sync_token '*' and resets the mirror. Todoist's full sync returns only active items, so completed sub-tasks are absent from the mirror; the parent's remote subs then differ from base and the pull overwrites the local subs, deleting every ticked sub-task. If the local subs were also edited, local wins, and each local sub whose x is no longer in the mirror is sent again as item_add, duplicating it in Todoist. Reproduced with a fake that, like Todoist, omits checked items from a full sync: 'Plan' (ticked) vanished locally after linking a second list. Depends on Todoist excluding completed sub-items from a full sync (documented behaviour for completed tasks).

title: Todoist: completing a repeating reminder here sends a new due string instead of closing the occurrence
evidence: exp/td.js recur → cmds [[{type:item_update,args:{id:T1,due:{date:'2026-11-05',string:'every week',is_recurring:true}}}]]; gym: local done=true, cmds [[item_close]]; js/core/reminders.js:229-236, js/core/exttasks.js:99-107, 282-290
rootCause: Local recurrence semantics duplicated instead of delegated to the provider that owns the rule.
fix: For a linked repeating reminder, push item_close (Todoist rolls the date itself) and let the pull bring the new date back; treat ext.rs rules as repeating in complete() (roll forward with Todoist as the source) so both paths behave alike.
detail: KOS.reminders.complete() rolls a repeating reminder forward locally (new due, done=false) so the push sees only a 'when' change and sends item_update with due {date: next, string: 'every week', is_recurring}. Todoist never records the completion (no history/karma, completed view empty), and since Todoist parses due.string, the explicit date may be ignored and re-anchored to today, which the next pull brings back. For a Todoist-only rule (ext.rs, e.g. 'every mon, fri') the reminder instead closes locally (recur is null here) and sends item_close, so it shows as completed until the next pull un-completes it with Todoist's new date: two different behaviours for the same action.

title: An assignment re-keyed by the cloud merge leaves its goals, Exams links, Focus sessions and review picks pointing at another assignment
evidence: js/core/cloudmerge.js:57-58 (assignments refs: calendar.events only), 293-346 (rekeyCollisions rewrites only spec.refs); references listed above
rootCause: Counter ids plus a hand-maintained reference list that new features did not extend.
fix: Add every reference to RECORDS[].refs (goals.items links.assignmentId as a nested field, exams.assessments links.assignmentId, sessions metrics.assignmentId and metrics.segments[].assignmentId, dayReview picks), or move assignments/reminders/events to random string ids as Money, Routines and Exams already do (the long-term fix).
detail: Ids are per-device counters; when two devices mint the same assignment id between syncs, rekeyCollisions re-keys the local one and rewrites only RECORDS[].refs. For assignments.items that list is calendar.events.assignmentId alone, but assignment ids are also stored in goals (links.assignmentId, js/core/goals.js:130), Exams assessments (links.assignmentId, js/core/exams.js:178, 536, 726), session entries and their segments (metrics.assignmentId, js/core/sessions.js:93-98; Focus banks minutes by it), and Daily Review picks (js/core/dayreview.js:489). After a re-key those references silently follow the OTHER device's assignment: minutes, goal progress and an exam's linked coursework attach to the wrong record. Reminders have the same gap (reminder ids referenced by the review picks).

title: A 404 on an update deletes the local event or reminder (e.g. after reconnecting a different Google account)
evidence: js/core/extgcal.js:419-421, js/core/exttasks.js:416-417, js/core/ext.js:241-250
rootCause: A failed write is treated as proof of a remote deletion.
fix: On 404 for an update, unlink the record (ext = null, keep it local, count it as 'unlinked' in the status) instead of deleting it; delete locally only from a pull that reports the item cancelled/deleted. Clear (or archive) ext links on disconnect and on connecting a different account (compare the account id).
detail: When a PATCH to Google Calendar or Google Tasks answers 404/410, the cycle deletes the LOCAL record inside inbound(): extgcal.js:421 KOS.calendar.deleteEvent(ev.id), exttasks.js:417 KOS.reminders.remove(it.id). disconnect() (ext.js:241-250) clears only the kv (sync tokens, mirrors) and leaves every record's ext link in place, so connecting a different Google account (or the event being moved to another calendar) turns the next local edit of any linked event or reminder into a silent local deletion, with no undo and no notice. This contradicts the 'never inferred from absence' intent of invariant 158 and is the opposite of Todoist's behaviour (an update to a missing item there is just retried forever, exttasks.js:330-333).

title: The full backup leaves out saved Reports and snapshots, and builds one giant string that can fail on the iPad
evidence: js/core/store.js:513-583 (no reportStore step; JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) at 588), js/core/reportstore.js (no exportAll), js/modules/attachments.js:454-480 (base64 for every blob)
rootCause: Backup coverage list maintained by hand; whole-document serialisation.
fix: Add KOS.reportStore.exportAll/importAll to the snapshot; stream the backup (build the Blob from parts: a JSON head plus one part per file, no indentation) or offer 'backup without files' when files exceed ~100 MB; report per-section failures like importFull does instead of failing the whole export.
detail: store.snapshotFull collects state, media, attachments (kurenai-os-files, every binary as base64), money, reviews, mind, ink and creatives, but not kurenai-os-reports (saved weeks/months/terms/years, their Kurenai words and the boundary snapshots that status moves need — 'never recomputed', invariant 101/102). Signed out, a restore on a new device loses every saved report and snapshot for good. The backup is serialised with JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) into a single Blob: with a few hundred MB of files (the app asks for persistent storage at 200 MB) the base64 plus indentation is a string of several hundred MB, which risks an out-of-memory reload on iPad Safari, and that failure is silent (no error reaches done()). A failing sub-export (e.g. creatives) aborts the whole backup instead of reporting the missing part.

title: The whole state lives in one localStorage key with no fallback: when it outgrows the quota every later change is lost on reload
evidence: kos.mjs eval 17 → state 372,924 chars; srs 110,391; sessions 84,052; pacing 84,696; 5,436 curriculum cards; quota experiment → errs ['Kurenai OS: save failed QuotaExceededError…'], stored:false, toast 'Save failed — storage may be full. Export your data.'; js/core/store.js:395-425
rootCause: Single-key localStorage persistence for an unbounded document.
fix: Move the large, append-heavy parts (srs/cards, the session ledger, Japanese facets, Mind cards) into IndexedDB records like the review log, or store the document in IndexedDB with localStorage as a small boot cache; show the state size in Archive › Storage with a warning at 60% of quota; on a failed save keep a persistent banner (not a toast) and retry into IndexedDB.
detail: Measured on the seeded account: the state document is 372,924 characters in one key (kurenai-os-v1); srs is 110 KB for 675 rated cards (164 B a card), sessions 84 KB for 600 (140 B each, capped at 2,000), pacing 85 KB. The curriculum alone has 5,436 flashcards, so a fully reviewed deck is ~0.9 MB before Code, Japanese facets and Mind cards, and every new domain adds to the same document. Chrome refused the write at ~5.2 M characters total; WebKit's limit is of the same order. When setItem throws, save() shows one toast ('Save failed — storage may be full. Export your data.') and keeps running on the in-memory copy; every later change, and the pagehide flush (which only logs, store.js:417-425), is lost on the next reload or when iOS evicts the page. Reproduced by filling localStorage on the slot: the save failed with QuotaExceededError and the change was not stored. There is no size readout in Archive › Storage for the state document, and no migration of the big parts (srs, sessions, facets) to IndexedDB.

title: Every replicated store pulls with a strict updated_at > cursor on now() stamps, so a row committed late is skipped forever
evidence: supabase/migrations/20260716000001_kos_sync_init.sql:26-35 (now()); q.gt('updated_at', …) at js/core/money.js:1126, reviewlog.js:133, mindjournal.js:191, inksync.js:97, reportstore.js:324, cloudsync.js:358/376; cursor = max seen (money.js:1189, 1207)
rootCause: Timestamp cursor over transaction-start timestamps.
fix: Stamp with clock_timestamp() in the trigger and pull with an overlap window (gt cursor − 2 minutes) — every store already skips its own echo by stamp or uid, so re-reading a few rows is harmless; or use a monotonic bigserial 'version' column per table as the cursor.
detail: Media, files, money, reviews, mind, ink, reports and push all pull 'updated_at > cursor' and then advance the cursor to the largest updated_at seen. The touch trigger stamps updated_at := now(), which in Postgres is the TRANSACTION START time. If device A's upsert (a 500-row media chunk, a money batch) starts at t1 and commits after device B's quicker write stamped t2 > t1, a third device that pulls between the two commits sets its cursor to t2 and never fetches A's rows (t1 < t2). Nothing ever re-reads them: the pulling device silently lacks those transactions/reviews/ink strokes until a restore. With three devices syncing on focus this is a real, if rare, divergence with no symptom.

title: Todoist: a command the server rejects is resent on every cycle forever, with no status shown
evidence: js/core/exttasks.js:329-334 (only the all-ok case is handled; errors in r.sync_status are dropped), js/core/exttasks.js:256 (delete queue entry kept on error)
rootCause: Error results of batched commands are ignored.
fix: Read sync_status errors: for 'not found' (error_code 22) drop the queue entry or unlink the record; for other errors record them in counts and setStatus so Connections shows 'n changes refused' with the reason; apply per-command bookkeeping rather than per group.
detail: tdPush applies a record's bookkeeping only when every command in its group returns 'ok'. A rejected command (item_update or item_delete for a task deleted or moved out of reach in Todoist, an invalid label, a due string Todoist cannot parse) leaves base and the delete queue unchanged, so the same command is sent every cycle (every few minutes and on every focus) and the Connections status still says the cycle succeeded, because sync_status errors are never turned into counts or an error. A partly-applied group (item_update ok, item_close rejected) also re-sends the parts that did apply.

title: An unreadable stored state is replaced by a fresh one and overwritten on the next save
evidence: js/core/store.js:382-390 (catch → DEFAULTS, console.warn only), 393 and 395-410 (save overwrites KEY)
rootCause: No quarantine of the original before the first overwrite.
fix: On a parse failure copy the raw string to a side key (kurenai-os-v1.corrupt-<ts>) or into IndexedDB before anything saves, and show a blocking notice offering Restore from backup / cloud.
detail: At boot, if JSON.parse or deepMerge of kurenai-os-v1 throws, the app logs a warning and starts from DEFAULTS; the next save() (any render that creates a progress record, the boot seeders) writes the empty state over the unreadable original, so whatever was recoverable from it is gone and the user is not told. With cloud sync the empty-local guard then adopts the cloud copy, but a signed-out user loses everything silently.

title: Backup & Restore's 'What a backup covers' list is out of date: half of what the file holds, and everything it leaves out, is unlisted
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/data-integrity/data-mac.png; list text read via eval; js/core/store.js:513-583 (what snapshotFull includes)
rootCause: Hand-written copy that did not follow the backup's growth.
fix: Generate the rows from the same table snapshotFull uses (one row per store with its live count), and add a short 'Not in the file' line naming Reports, the Paper library and connections.
detail: The list names study, productivity, Governor, the media vault, the purchase planner and attachments. The file also carries Money transactions, the review log, handwriting, Mind's Journal and Creatives work, none of which is listed; and it does NOT carry saved Reports and snapshots, the Paper library's own PDFs (unless kept in the cloud), Japanese saved lines, or the Google/Todoist sign-ins (records stay linked but need reconnecting) — the reader is not told. The closing line points only to 'Sync & Import' for reconnecting, not Connections.

title: Archive › Storage accounts for none of the app's real data and prints rows of 0 KB
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/data-integrity/storage-mac.png, audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/data-integrity/storage-iphone.png
rootCause: Storage page written for Files R4 only.
fix: List every store (state document with its share of the localStorage quota, media vault, money, reviews, ink, mind, creatives, reports, files, papers, text index) with sizes from navigator.storage.estimate().usageDetails or a count × average, hide zero rows, and let the last card span the row.
detail: On the seeded account (1,880 media entries, 373 KB state document, money, reviews) 'On this device' says 48.4 MB used while 'By kind of data' lists only Files, Past papers, Your ink and Text index, each '0 KB' — supporting zeros that invariant 77 says to suppress — and never shows the state document (the one store with a hard ~5 MB ceiling), the media vault, Money, the review log, Mind or Creatives. The numbers cannot explain the total. On the Mac the last card ('Not linked anywhere') sits alone in a row with two empty columns beside it.

title: Boot loads ~16.6 MB of JavaScript in 340 synchronous script tags, most of it curriculum content no first view needs
devices: all; worst on iPhone 17 and iPad (cold launch of the Home Screen app)
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/arch/prof-boot-empty.txt; index.html lines 48-55 (only defer tags) and the 340-script list; sizes via stat: exam-index.js 566,954 B, code-projects-files.js 382,808 B, it-f204.js 299,469 B, hub.js 232,148 B, aitools.js 208,176 B; Performance API: domInteractive 14,993 ms, longtasks 61 / 15,441 ms; dense account warm reload (SW controlling, V8 code cache): data-shell=ready at 21,064 ms, 35 long tasks totalling 19,166 ms, heap 58 MB (machine shared with other audit slots, load avg ~5)
rootCause: Classic script-tag design (chosen so file:// works) with no lazy-loading layer; every new study space appended its whole content to index.html.
fix: Keep the script-tag architecture but split content into lazily loaded bundles: KOS.content.get(key) already funnels every read, so make content files register a loader per subject/unit (a tiny manifest listing keys -> file) and inject the script on first open of a topic, a desk or search (search can use a prebuilt title/keyword index). Load exam-index.js only on #/exams, code-projects-files.js only on export, ja/mind/creatives content only when their desk opens. Target: boot payload under ~4 MB. Also add performance.mark('kos-boot-start'/'kos-interactive') in main.js so the cost is tracked by a smoke test budget.
detail: index.html lists 340 <script src> tags; only KaTeX, supabase.js and env.local.js are deferred. Summed on disk: 16.64 MB JS (js/data/content 8.28 MB in 126 files, js/modules 3.33 MB, js/core 2.50 MB, js/data 1.67 MB, js/labs 0.60 MB) plus 1.21 MB CSS in 24 sheets. Every topic's notes for every subject (CS, Maths, IT, Code units 1-12, tracks, Japanese, Mind, Creatives), the 567 KB past-paper index, and the 383 KB Rider project scaffolds (code-projects-files.js, needed only when exporting a Rider zip) are parsed and executed before Home renders. In the harness a cold reload of the EMPTY account took 15.0 s to domInteractive with 61 long tasks totalling 15.4 s (max 2.75 s); the CPU profile shows 11 s of (program) (parse/compile) and the top self-time scripts are content files executing their builders (cs-p2-46b.js 746 ms, code.js lesson() 316 ms, cs-p2-411.js 545 ms, cs-p2-410a.js 497 ms, maths-stats-s4 325 ms...). The machine was shared with other audit slots so absolute times are inflated, but the shape is unambiguous: the content payload dominates boot, and on an iPad/iPhone (slower JS, tighter memory, Safari evicting a backgrounded Home Screen app) every cold launch pays it. Heap after boot on the empty account: 68 MB.

title: This audit's checkout is 23 commits behind origin/main: the harness serves sw kos-creatives-1, not production's kos-artshop-1

title: Cold-path cost after boot: the first render of each heavy view takes 0.5-2.8 s on the dense account (Exams, Code map, Due, Pacing, Calendar), then 20-200 ms
devices: all; most felt on iPhone 17 and iPad cold launches
evidence: eval timings above (slot 18, seeded); audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/arch/prof-boot-dense.txt (readiness js/core/exams.js:635 1314 ms self in the boot profile, exams.js:945 predictPass 893 ms), arch/prof-code.txt, arch/prof-calendar.txt; js/core/code.js:166-190, 856-895; js/modules/code.js:417-490; js/modules/calendar.js:546-570, 1762-1800; js/core/exams.js:635-720, 943-960
rootCause: Pure derive-on-read design (a good contract) without any memoisation layer, so composite pages multiply the cost; plus eager loading of all code.
fix: Add a cheap per-tick memo: a KOS.store revision counter bumped by save(), and memoise the heavy pure reads (exams.readiness/leaves, code stats/unitState/pageCount, calendar derivedOn for a month range, srs.allCards) on (args, revision, day). Shipped content is immutable at runtime (invariant 86), so pageCount/listingsOf can be cached forever. For the calendar, compute derived items for the visible range once and bucket by date. Pair with lazy content loading (boot finding) to cut compile cost.
detail: Rendering each view three times in a row (via a cheap view in between) on the seeded account gave: exams 2750/589/179 ms, code map 1622/504/355, due 1623/263/22, pacing 1405/51/120, calendar 1015/168/189, japanese 825/59/311, routines 705/11/16, mind 670/171/126, home 205/175/63 (first ever Home after boot was 2.0-3.3 s). Steady state is acceptable; the first visit after a cold launch is not, and on an iPad/iPhone Home Screen app every relaunch after Safari evicts it is a cold launch. Two causes: (1) V8 lazily compiles functions from the 16.6 MB of eagerly loaded script on first use, and (2) the derived reads have no per-render snapshot, so first calls are expensive and repeated: KOS.exams.readiness over 17 assessments measured 3,247 ms then 696/78/55 ms on later runs; KOS.code.unitState (js/core/code.js:888) rescans every lesson and calls stats() (code.js:856) per call, and the Code map (js/modules/code.js:417-490) calls it per unit, per track need (needMet) and per track section (trackState); evidence() re-splits shipped notes with KOS.content.splitPages on every call (code.js:168, 66 ms/call measured). The Calendar month calls dayItems -> derivedOn (37 ms/call warm, calendar.js:563) for each of 35-42 cells, re-reading every Money rule, goal and exam start-by per cell.

title: Detached pages leak: global listeners are removed only when their event next fires, so every visited topic/Files/lesson page stays in memory
devices: iPad (long-lived Home Screen app) and iPhone most; all
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/arch/mem.txt, arch/mem2.txt; eval: 5 paste listeners after 5 Files visits; grep 'isConnected[^;]*removeEventListener' = 15 sites listed
rootCause: No view lifecycle: KOS.show replaces #main with innerHTML='' and has no unmount step, so each module invented a lazy self-removal.
fix: Give KOS.show a teardown hook: views register cleanups via a KOS.ui.onLeave(fn) (or an AbortController per render, passing {signal} to addEventListener) that KOS.show calls before clearing #main; replace the 15 lazy removals with it. Add a smoke check that navigating 20 views leaves the listener count flat (jsdom can count via a wrapped addEventListener).
detail: 15 places add a window/document listener on each render and remove it lazily inside the handler ('if (!node.isConnected) { removeEventListener(...); return; }'): hub.js:2719 and 3169 (kos-ink on every topic page), files.js:283 (paste) and 292 (kos-files-index), attachments.js:736 (paste), inkui.js:1422 (keydown), inktab.js:518, codetopic.js:214/228, jatopic.js:321/334, mindtopic.js:380/395, crtopic.js:246, inksync.js:339. Rare events (kos-ink fires only when ink is written; paste only on a paste) never come, so each closure keeps its whole detached page alive. Measured with forced GC (CDP HeapProfiler.collectGarbage + Memory.getDOMCounters) on the seeded account: on Files, 9,003 DOM nodes / 886 listeners; after opening 30 CS topic pages and returning to Files, 24,954 nodes / 2,369 listeners (about 16,000 detached nodes retained); dispatching one kos-ink event dropped it to 11,027 / 1,096. Three rounds over 23 views grew nodes from 1,786 to 14,110 and listeners from 157 to 1,795. Opening Files 5 times adds 5 document paste listeners. On an iPad Home Screen app kept open for days this is unbounded growth until Safari kills the page (which then pays the full cold boot).

title: KOS.rerender() drops keyboard focus to <body> on every redraw, including background ones (cloud pull, habit auto-tick)
devices: Mac (keyboard), iPad with keyboard, VoiceOver on all
evidence: eval on slot 18: {home:{ms:225,focusedBefore:'home.review-line',after:'BODY'}, calendar:{ms:326,after:'BODY'}, routines, reminders, money all BODY}; js/core/ui.js:344-357; js/core/cloudsync.js:723-731; js/core/routines.js:699
rootCause: Redraw is implemented as navigation (rebuild #main) with only scroll restoration.
fix: In KOS.rerender, before the redraw record the focused element's identity inside #main (closest [data-ui] plus data-key/data-id/aria-label and its index among matches) and after it focus the equivalent node with {preventScroll:true}, falling back to #main without announcing; skip background redraws while focus is inside #main and the user is typing (or defer them until blur).
detail: Invariant 65 says a redraw changes no focus. KOS.rerender (js/core/ui.js:344-357) re-runs KOS.show(..., {_nav:true}), which empties #main (ui.js, main.innerHTML = '') and rebuilds it; it restores main.scrollTop but not the focused control. Measured on the seeded account: focusing a control and calling KOS.rerender() left document.activeElement = BODY on Home (was home.review-line), Calendar (cal.mode), Routines (ui.tab), Reminders (rem.side-item) and Money (ui.tab). Background callers make this hit keyboard and VoiceOver users without any action of theirs: cloudsync.js:731 rerenderCurrent after a pull, routines.js:699 after autoSync ticks a habit, plus 142 KOS.rerender() call sites in total (most after the user's own action, where the control they used vanishes). A redraw also costs a full view build (225 ms Home, 326 ms Calendar warm).

title: iPhone: most text fields and selects are under 16px, so iOS Safari zooms the page on every focus
evidence: css/base.css:156-160 (rule inside @layer base); css/tokens.css:35 (@layer tokens, base, layout, components, views, themes); overriding rules e.g. css/components.css:406 .k-input, :417 .k-pill-select font-size var(--fs-12-5), css/views/assistant.css:216 .k-asst-input font-size var(--fs-14-5); measurement audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/a11y-iphone.jsonl (font16 lists per view, script a11y-scan.js)

fix: Move the phone 16px rule to the last layer (themes, or an unlayered rule at the end of components.css) so it wins: @media (max-width:700px){ input:not([type=checkbox]):not([type=radio]):not([type=range]), select, textarea, [contenteditable] { font-size: max(16px, 1em) !important } } — or set --fs-input tokens that components read. That rule lives in @layer base, which the declared order (tokens, base, layout, components, views, themes) puts BELOW every component and view rule, so any class that sets a font size wins. title: Focus chime is silent on iPhone/iPad and has no on/off or volume setting
evidence: js/modules/focus.js:788-801 (chime(): new AC() on first call from tick, no ctx.resume()); call sites :496, :508, :522 inside the interval tick; grep -rniE '"(Sound|Chime)' js/modules js/core → none
rootCause: Audio unlock rules of iOS WebKit not handled; no audio preference model.
fix: Create/resume the AudioContext in Start's click handler (unlock it), call ctx.resume() before each chime, and add a Focus setting 'Sound at cycle end' (on/off + volume, per device in state.ui). Also send a device notification for cycle end when the page is hidden.
detail: The only sound in the app (Pomodoro cycle end, break end, stopwatch break nudge) is a Web Audio oscillator whose AudioContext is created lazily inside the timer tick, never from a user gesture and never resume()d. WebKit starts such a context 'suspended', so on the user's iPhone and iPad the chime never plays; the cue is then only a 2.6 s toast that a user away from the screen will miss. There is also no setting anywhere to turn the chime off, choose a sound or set its volume (grep finds no Sound/Chime control). Japanese voice lines and the Assistant's speech are the only other audio.

title: Status chips fail AA contrast app-wide (3.5–4.3:1 at 11.5px), worst in Atelier Dawn
evidence: css/components.css:191-199 (.k-chip: color var(--chip-c); background color-mix(var(--chip-c) 18%, transparent)); scan output audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/a11y-mac-dawn2.jsonl and a11y-mac.jsonl (script audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/a11y-scan.js); token ratios computed: Dawn --red on --s1 5.78, on its own wash 3.68
rootCause: Chip ink is the same role token as its wash; tokens were tuned for page ground, not for the tinted chip.
fix: Give chips an ink variant per role: text = oklch(from var(--chip-c) calc(l - 0.12) c h) in Dawn (calc(l + 0.08) in dark themes), or keep the role colour for a dot and set the label in --text-2. Add a smoke check that every [data-tone] chip ≥ 4.5:1 in Graphite and Dawn.
detail: Every .k-chip paints its text in the role colour on an 18% wash of the same colour. The wash darkens/lightens the ground towards the text, so the role colours that pass on the page (4.5–5.8:1, computed from the tokens) drop below 4.5:1 on their own chip. Measured on the seeded account (Mac, real theme via KOS.governor.setTheme): Dawn — Assignments 'Overdue' 3.68, vault 'In progress' 3.52–3.62, Wishlist '◆ Priority purchase' 3.36, '#urgent' 4.02, 'Medium' 4.04, '23 behind' 4.04, Governor '● All systems open' 3.96; Graphite — 'Overdue' 3.93, 'Coursework / NEA' 4.28, 'Not enough evidence' 3.94, 'recall 94%' 3.94, 'Too early to call' 3.94. These are the app's most decision-relevant labels (overdue, at risk) and are 11.5px, regular weight.

title: Touch-size floor is undone by shared primitives: pill selects 30px, switches 34x20, checkboxes 18x18 on iPad and iPhone
evidence: css/base.css:115-121 (:where(...) floor; no input[type=checkbox], no .k-switch); css/components.css:417 (.k-pill-select { min-block-size: 0 } cancels it); css/components.css:207 (.k-switch fixed --fx-switch-w/h, not in the coarse block at :669-677); css/layout.css:233-235 (.k-rail-toggle at --hit-dense); measurements audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/a11y-ipad.jsonl, a11y-iphone.jsonl
rootCause: The floor is a zero-specificity base rule; primitives set their own sizes after it.
fix: In the components coarse block add: .k-pill-select { min-block-size: var(--hit-coarse) }; .k-switch { scale or an inset ::before hit area to 44x44 } (keep the visual 34x20 but pad the label/row); input[type=checkbox]:not(.k-switch) { inline-size/block-size 24px plus a 44px label hit area }; remove min-block-size:0 from .k-pill-select. A smoke check over every view at pointer:coarse for interactive boxes < 44px would stop the regressions.
detail: base.css gives every button/select/text input a 44px min-height under (pointer: coarse), but with zero specificity, and several SHARED primitives cancel or bypass it, so the same defect shows up on every page (other areas reported page instances; this is the common root cause). Measured on iPad (820x1180, touch) and iPhone: .k-pill-select 30px tall everywhere it is used (Assignments filters, Exams & Papers, Shrine/Wishlist/vault sort, topic reader select, Card stats); .k-switch 34x20 (Notifications ×5, Pen and ink ×4, Storage, Routines settings ×10, Focus 'Penalise tab-switches', Media Sync auto, Exams season/quiet); native checkboxes 18x18 (Pacing lesson ticks, Wishlist plan.check, tracker k-box, Files ink filter, Home habit tick input); the rail collapse toggle 24x24; scroller arrows 32x32; Reports Share/Export 32px; Card stats retention inputs 30px.
