title: Backspace on any focused button navigates Back, even inside an open dialog, leaving the dialog over a different page
evidence: js/main.js:20-29 (keydown: !typing && key === 'Backspace' → KOS.back(), no dialog/overlay check); repro via eval: before '#/calendar', after '#/home', dialogStill true; shots/a11y-hci/backspace-under-dialog-mac.png; js/modules/help.js:299 shortcut list
rootCause: Global shortcut written before dialogs were overlays rendered outside the router's control.
fix: Drop the bare Backspace binding (keep Alt+←/→ and the buttons), or at least ignore it when a [role=dialog][aria-modal=true], the Focus overlay, a review sheet or the Exam Room is open and when focus is inside #main controls.
detail: main.js treats a bare Backspace outside text fields as 'Back'. Keyboard users routinely have focus on a button (after clicking Cancel/Done/a rating, or tabbing), so a stray Backspace — e.g. meant to correct a field they thought was focused — leaves the page. The handler does not check for an open dialog: reproduced on the Calendar's New event modal with focus on Cancel; Backspace changed the route #/calendar → #/home and the modal stayed open, kicker 'Calendar', floating over Home. Browsers removed Backspace-as-Back for exactly this data-loss reason; Help & Guide does not list it (it lists Alt ← / →).

title: The document title never changes: every page is 'Kurenai OS — Study Atelier'
evidence: index.html:6; grep document.title → only js/modules/focus.js:1070,1488; eval on 9 routes: title='Kurenai OS — Study Atelier' for all
rootCause: Single-page shell with no title owner.
fix: In router.js after each KOS.show, set document.title = '<page h1 or nav label> · <section> — KurenaiOS' (topic: '<ref> <title> · CS'); Focus keeps prefixing the remaining time.
detail: No view sets document.title; only Focus writes it (the countdown, then back to the default). So the browser tab, the history list (long-press Back, Mac History menu), Mac window/tab switcher, bookmarks, and screen-reader page announcements all read the same name on Home, a topic, Money or a vault (WCAG 2.4.2 Page Titled). The router already knows the view and its label (KOS.currentNav), and the phone title bar computes the page title.

title: No haptic or tactile-equivalent feedback anywhere on iPhone/iPad
evidence: grep -rn vibrate js css sw.js → no matches
rootCause: No feedback-channel policy beyond toasts.
fix: Add navigator.vibrate guarded calls for Android/desktop PWAs and, for iOS, make timer events post a local notification (already have the notify path) and keep the cue on screen until acknowledged.
detail: Nothing in the app calls navigator.vibrate or offers any haptic substitute. On the user's touch devices the moments that would warrant one — a Focus cycle ending, the idle-watch warning, a flashcard rating, a routine completing, an unlock — rely on sound (silent on iOS, see the chime finding) or a short toast. iOS Safari does not support navigator.vibrate, so the practical substitute is a stronger, longer-lived visual cue plus a device notification for timer events while the page is hidden.

title: Error toasts show raw exception text ('Save failed: <err.message>')
evidence: js/modules/medview.js:594,1031,1049,1245; js/core/files.js:310; js/modules/files.js:108; js/modules/assignments.js:271; js/modules/governor-ui.js:876; js/modules/attachments.js:707,993
rootCause: No shared error-message helper.
fix: Route errors through one helper (KOS.ui.failToast(action, err)) mapping known errors (quota, offline, permission) to a plain sentence with a next step; log the raw message to the console only. Pick one contraction style.
detail: Ten error toasts concatenate err.message directly (IndexedDB/DOMException or fetch messages such as 'QuotaExceededError' text or 'Failed to fetch'), with no explanation or next step; elsewhere the app uses calm sentences ('Couldn't save it on this device.'). Wording is also split between 'Couldn't' and 'Could not' across 16+ toasts.

title: Calendar dialogs float their Cancel/Close button in the middle of the footer

title: Reduced motion is not honoured by JS smooth scrolling
evidence: js/core/ui.js:693; js/modules/hub.js:2874,2996; js/modules/codetopic.js:296,382; js/modules/jatopic.js:234; js/modules/mindtopic.js:292; js/modules/crtopic.js:176; js/modules/inktab.js:204; js/modules/examguide.js:109; js/modules/reportlong.js:441; js/modules/mobile-shell.js:120; css/base.css:163-169; duplicated reduced() helpers js/core/jaui.js:28, js/core/mindui.js:25, js/modules/assistant.js:250, js/modules/reportstory.js:474, js/modules/examroom.js:88
rootCause: No shared motion helper; CSS reset cannot reach explicit JS behaviour.
fix: Add KOS.ui.reducedMotion() and KOS.ui.scrollBehavior() ('auto' when reduced) in ui.js; replace the literal 'smooth' and the five private helpers with it.
detail: base.css forces scroll-behavior:auto under prefers-reduced-motion, but that only affects CSS-driven scrolling. Twelve call sites pass behavior:'smooth' explicitly to scrollIntoView/scrollBy/scrollTo, which the browser animates regardless: every topic page turn in CS/Maths/IT, Code, Japanese, Mind and Creatives lessons (the article scrolls to its top), the shared scroller's arrow paging, the phone section strip, the Exams guide's section jump, the ink tab and the long report pages. Only the Assistant, report story, Japanese/Mind scenes and Exam Room check the media query themselves (each with its own copy of the helper).

title: iPhone Assignments shows its title twice (phone title bar plus the page's own header)

title: Inconsistent button wording: two plus glyphs, an empty state naming a button that does not exist

title: Tab strips declare role=tablist/tab but ignore arrow keys and have no tabpanel
evidence: js/core/ui.js:495 (role tab, aria-selected), :515 (role tablist); no Arrow handling in js/core/ui.js tabs or js/core/a11y.js; eval on #/routines: ArrowRight → focus stays 'Today', tabindexes [0,0,0,0,0], aria-controls all null; other role=tablist sites: js/engines/flashcards.js, js/modules/assistant.js, medview.js, code.js, dayreview.js, hub.js, coderider.js, codetopic.js, codecap.js, governor-ui.js, js/labs/oop.js
rootCause: ARIA roles added without the keyboard behaviour they imply; hand-made strips copy the roles.
fix: Either drop role=tab/tablist (these switch views, so plain buttons with aria-pressed or aria-current fit) or implement the pattern once in KOS.ui.tabs: roving tabindex, Left/Right/Home/End, aria-controls to the panel the page renders.
detail: KOS.ui.tabs (workspace and card variants) and ~11 hand-made strips mark their buttons role='tab' with aria-selected, so VoiceOver announces 'tab, 1 of 5' and the ARIA pattern promises Left/Right arrows. Nothing implements them: on Routines' strip, ArrowRight on the selected tab leaves focus on 'Today'; every tab stays tabindex 0 (no roving focus), and no tab has aria-controls / no region has role=tabpanel. Keyboard users must Tab through every tab, and screen-reader users are told to use keys that do nothing.

title: iPad Calendar: every day cell carries an invisible '+' (New event) that a tap can hit
evidence: css/views/productivity.css:470-471 (opacity 0; shown on .k-cal-cell:hover / :focus-visible), :890 (phone: display none), :961-963 (hover:none block lists .k-rem-del, .k-hb-del, .k-pace-move only); eval at 820x1180 touch: matchMedia('(hover: none)') true, .k-cal-add opacity '0', label 'New event on Mon 26 Oct'
rootCause: Hover-reveal pattern applied without the touch override used elsewhere.
fix: Add .k-cal-add to the productivity.css hover:none block (opacity 1, muted) or remove it on touch and rely on the header's '+ New event' with the tapped day preselected.
detail: The month grid's per-day '+' (.k-cal-add, aria-label 'New event on <day>') is opacity 0 until :hover or :focus-visible. Unlike Reminders' delete, Pacing's move and the topic's row buttons, it has no (hover: none) override, so on the iPad (touch, no hover, wider than the phone tier where it is display:none) it is never visible yet stays a live 24x24 target in each cell's top-right corner: the feature cannot be discovered, and a tap aimed at the cell's date lands on an invisible button and opens the New event dialog.

title: Goals opens on a blank page (no loading state) until the async compute returns
evidence: js/modules/goals.js:306-309 (empty page then G.compute(callback)); eval sampling every 400ms after KOS.show('goals') at 820x1180: ['0/0','0/0','1085/3',…]; shots/a11y-hci/goals-ipad.png (blank, 2.5s after navigation) vs shots/a11y-hci/goals-ipad2.png (filled); shots/resp/820x1180-atelier-dawn-goals.jpg blank

On the seeded account at iPad size the container was 0px high with no children for 0.8-1.2s after navigation (2.5s+ on a cold load: the responsive audit's iPad screenshot captured an empty Goals page). title: Help & Guide describes screens that no longer exist, and its last section has no mark

The shortcut card omits Backspace-as-Back (see the Backspace finding). title: Calendar's leading/trailing days fade their events to ~2.3-2.9:1 while they stay clickable
evidence: eval on #/calendar: first cal.ev-t 'Revision block 28' 2.87 (Graphite) / 2.28 (Dawn) with ancestor k-cal-stack opacity 0.4; css/views/productivity.css:465 (other-month stack 0.75 on hover/focus-within); scan a11y-mac.jsonl, a11y-mac-dawn2.jsonl
rootCause: Opacity applied to the whole stack including interactive text.
fix: Dim the day number and cell ground instead of the events (e.g. date in --muted, events at full contrast with a muted dot), or keep opacity ≥ 0.7 so text stays ≥ 4.5:1.
detail: Cells from the previous/next month put their event stack at opacity 0.4 (0.75 on hover/focus-within). Event chips there are still full buttons (they open the event), but their 11px titles measure 2.87:1 in Graphite and 2.28:1 in Dawn, and the day number 1.2-1.45:1. On the iPad there is no hover to raise them. A week that straddles months (e.g. 26 Oct-1 Nov on the November grid) shows half its week this way.
